performed_via_github_app.description:
Publish incredibly high performance websites and applications right from GitHub. The Netlify platform connects your repositories to an all-in-one workflow for global CDN deployment, continuous integration, and automatic (and free) HTTPS. Each time you commit changes, Netlify builds your site, prerenders markup, and optimizes assets on dedicated build infrastructure. Easily create an entirely automated workflows for your web applications

## Features

### Push your site live, directly from GitHub
Deploy your site to an ultra-redundant global CDN that’s purpose built for serving pages and assets quickly and consistently.

### Automate deployment
Netlify’s built-in Continuous Deployment automatically runs your build commands and deploys the result whenever you push to your Git repository.

### Add a custom domain
Purchase domains and manage DNS zones and records right inside of Netlify.

### HTTPS is automatic
Your site will automatically be secured with a free TLS certificate from Let’s Encrypt.

### Deploy Previews
Netlify’s Deploy Previews streamlined your workflow by giving you a unique, permanent URL to check what your changes will be like in production whenever you submit a pull request.

### And a lot more!
Netlify includes solutions for forms, identity, and even custom functions powered by AWS Lambda. And all this functionality can be configured directly in your repo.

## Codex Review

### Overview
This PR fixes the nested-tooltip flicker reported in [#4499](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/issues/4499) by preventing a parent tooltip from opening, or staying open, while the pointer is over an enabled nested trigger. It does that by adding a nested-trigger guard in the tooltip hover path, closing hover-opened ancestors on nested trigger entry, and documenting/testing the new behavior.

### Findings (None)
No blocking issues found in this patch.

I reviewed the hover-delay path in `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useHoverReferenceInteraction.ts`, the nested-trigger event handling in `packages/react/src/tooltip/trigger/TooltipTrigger.tsx`, and the added delayed-hover regression coverage in `packages/react/src/tooltip/root/TooltipRoot.test.tsx`, and I did not find a remaining correctness issue in the current branch state.

### Confidence: 4/5
High confidence. The branch includes targeted coverage for the key delayed-hover sequence where the pointer enters the outer trigger first and then moves onto the nested trigger before the delay expires. Residual risk is limited to the usual complexity around hover timing and composed event flow.

### Notes
- The PR conversation appears to contain only bot comments, so there is no outstanding human review feedback to reconcile.

I believe we have to resort to checking the `closest()` DOM element (with the help of the custom data attribute), as we can't rely on accessing the other Trigger's store from the outside. I improved how it behaves with shadow DOM.

I also simplified the implementation and now use just a single call in `onMouseOver` to detect a nested trigger.

As for `useHoverReferenceInteraction` - the `shouldOpen` is an optional callback with zero overhead when not provided (`shouldOpenRef.current?.() !== false` short-circuits), aside from a couple of extra bytes in the bundle (less than 30 gzipped for components that don't use it). I believe it's the minimal and most readable way to prevent pending delayed opens before they happen.
